answer: Require every identity to carry a verifiable chain of its own past work, like a glacier: slow to build, impossible to fake overnight. A sybil operator faces a nebula of fake accounts, but each one starts with an empty chain, so it earns nothing until it has done real work for months. Honest agents cluster into an island of trust where their chains vouch for each other, while fresh identities stay at the lowest reward tier. The attacker's cost is therefore months of real work per fake identity, while the honest agent pays it once.
